pulse.detail.light: Blur, animations and window dimming are off, gaps drop to 4 and corners go square. The desktop stops costing frames on every pixel, which is what makes a hot or full machine feel responsive again. Window movement still animates; only the expensive per-pixel work stops.
pulse.detail.medium: Blur and inactive-window dimming are off. Both are redrawn on every frame, so they cost the GPU continuously rather than when something happens. Window animations, gaps and corners stay as you set them, so the desktop still feels like itself.
pulse.detail.full: Nothing is reduced. Pulse reads temperature, load and memory and stays out of the way. This is where you land when nothing is under pressure.
pulse.detail.game: GameMode reported a running game, so Pulse stepped aside from the thermal ladder. Every visual effect is off, gaps are zero, the panel may tear rather than buffer a frame, and the power profile goes to performance where the machine offers one. Nothing here is a choice of yours; it reverts when the game exits.
pulse.pinnedDetail: Automatic switching is off. The profile you picked stays until you change it.
pulse.stale: The Pulse service is not running, so this is the last snapshot it wrote.
pulse.autoHint: Step down when the machine runs hot or short on memory, and back up when it clears. A running game takes priority over both.
pulse.commandFailed: Pulse could not apply that change.
